facts.statement: Crichtonpelta was a herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur that lived in China during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Crichtonpelta is a genus of extinct herbivorous ankylosaurid dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Cenomanian) of China.

facts.statement: The species originally described in 2007 was named Crichtonsaurus benxiensis by Lü Junchang, Ji Qiang, Gao Yubo, and Li Zhixin.
facts.quote: In 2007, Lü Junchang, Ji Qiang, Gao Yubo and Li Zhixin named and described a second species of Crichtonsaurus: Crichtonsaurus benxiensis.

facts.statement: The genus name Crichtonpelta honors author Michael Crichton and the Greek word for a small shield.
facts.quote: The generic name combines a reference to Michael Crichton, the author of Jurassic Park, with a Greek πέλτη, peltè, "small shield".

facts.statement: The genus was validly established in 2015 by Victoria Arbour and Philip John Currie.
facts.quote: However, in 2015, Crichtonpelta was validly named by Arbour and Philip John Currie.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen BXGMV0012 is a skull found near Beipiao in the Sunjiawan Formation, dating to approximately 99–95 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype, BXGMV0012, is a skull found near Beipiao in a layer of the Sunjiawan Formation probably dating from the early Cenomanian (~99–95 Ma).

facts.statement: Victoria Arbour created the separate genus Crichtonpelta in 2014 because she considered the original genus Crichtonsaurus to be a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: In 2014, Victoria Arbour concluded that Crichtonsaurus were a nomen dubium. Therefore, she named a separate genus for its second species: Crichtonpelta.

facts.statement: A unique derived trait of Crichtonpelta is that the apex of its cheek horn points upwards.
facts.quote: One of these was an autapomorphy, unique derived trait: the apex of the (quadrato)jugal, or cheek, horn, is pointing upwards.

facts.statement: The armor on the upper snout of Crichtonpelta formed an amorphous mass rather than distinct tiles.
facts.quote: The upper snout armour forms an amorphous mass, not clearly separated into distinctive tiles.

facts.statement: The holotype of Crichtonpelta was somewhat larger than Crichtonsaurus, which measured about 3 to 4 meters in length.
facts.quote: The holotype of Crichtonpelta is somewhat larger than Crichtonsaurus, itself about 3 to 4 m long.

facts.statement: It is currently uncertain whether Crichtonpelta possessed a tail club.
facts.quote: It is uncertain whether the animal already possessed a tail club.

facts.statement: Crichtonpelta is classified within the subfamily Ankylosaurinae of the family Ankylosauridae.
facts.quote: Crichtonpelta was, within the Ankylosauridae, placed in the Ankylosaurinae, in a basal position.

facts.statement: If its basal position within Ankylosaurinae is correct, Crichtonpelta would be the oldest known ankylosaurine.
facts.quote: If correct, this makes it the oldest known ankylosaurine.

facts.statement: The fossil record for Crichtonpelta spans from the Albian to the Turonian stages, between 106.3 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Turonian (106.3 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is a possibility that fossil material previously referred to Crichtonsaurus bohlini actually belongs to Crichtonpelta.
facts.quote: There was a possibility that, though Crichtonsaurus bohlini was a nomen dubium, its fossil material in fact belonged to Crichtonpelta.

rejected.statement: Crichtonpelta lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 98 and 90 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
rejected.quote: Crichtonpelta benxiensis... vivió a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 98 y 90 millones de años, entre el Cenomaniense y Turoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.
